title: Three Marylebone Houses, a 56-Year Lease and a Promise to Pay
conflicts: Start year: EBSCO says 1864; Hill's letters show the plan agreed in 1864 and the purchase completed by 2 April 1865, matching English Heritage, Victorian Web and CIH (1865); story uses both steps. Later expansion: CIH says five more houses a year later, Hill's May 1866 letter says six more; story gives no number. The five per cent condition rests on a family account (English Heritage says only 'a small profit'); attributed to her family. Outcome figures (5% paid, £48 repaid, £2 11s 3d bad debts) are Hill's own 1866 report and are attributed to her. English Heritage calls the houses 'almost new'; Hill says well built but filthy; story follows Hill.
notes: Primary sources are Hill's own 1866 essay and her letters (both on Project Gutenberg). The slate's industry 'construction' was changed to housing (property management), which is what the episode is. One letter in the 1913 Life appears misdated (15 April 1865) and was not relied on. Stance: affirms.
